item.title: Real Madrid superstar returns to form in style with sensational brace for Brazil
item.description: Real Madrid superstar returns to form in style with sensational brace for Brazil Real Madrid have enjoyed an excellent run of results under Jose Mourinho, with several key attacking stars chipping in for Los Blancos . However, one player whose form has left a lot to be desired is Vinicius Jr., with the Brazilian struggling to get going this season . In his absence through a four-match suspension, Madrid have continued to improve and have looked like a more balanced side. However, the Brazilian offered an encouraging reminder of his quality on Saturday, scoring twice in his nation’s dramatic 3-2 defeat against Japan. Vinicius ends goalscoring drought with two stunning strikes The 26-year-old left winger has endured a frustrating spell in front of goal, with his lack of goals becoming particularly glaring. His overall performances have also been a cause for concern. However, against Japan, he looked considerably sharper. With Brazil trailing 2-0, the Madrid winger produced a spectacular long-range effort in the 33rd minute to pull his side back into contention. He struck again in the 75th minute, curling another excellent shot in off the post to restore parity. His influence extended well beyond the two goals. Vinicius created two big chances and registered five passes into the final third. Vinicius also completed four of his five attempted long balls. He delivered two crosses from three attempts, won four fouls and completed 32 carries. However, the Real Madrid star’s display was not enough to save Brazil from defeat, with Japan scoring a stoppage-time winner. A timely confidence boost for Mourinho’s Madrid Vinicius’ timely performance could prove to be an important turning point in his career. Even though he could not help his team secure victory on the night, he will take a lot of confidence from the performance. Vinicius has served his four-match suspension at Real Madrid. (Photo by Koji Watanabe/Getty Images) Having served his four-match suspension following his red card against Villarreal, he will be raring to go for Real Madrid after the break. It remains to be seen how Jose Mourinho handles Vinicius’ minutes in the coming weeks and manages the competition between him and Diomande. Vinicius’ return to form is exactly what the manager would have wanted from this international break, and the onus is now on the player to carry this momentum into the return of club football.

item.title: Adam Schefter drops bombshell Lamar Jackson injury twist for Ravens
item.description: Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images Adam Schefter drops bombshell Lamar Jackson injury twist for Ravens appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter gave an injury update on Lamar Jackson and his thumb injury. According to Minter, injuries like the one Jackson suffered and require surgery usually take 6-10 weeks to heal. But as ESPN’s Adam Schefter has reported, Jackson had already undergone thumb surgery last week . That means if Jackson meets the lower end of Minter’s specified timeline, he would still be able to return later this season. Jackson suffered the thumb injury in the very first snap of their 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Nov. 1. That was his first game back after missing a month due to a hamstring injury. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Ravens, who were 3-1 with Jackson as the starter in their first four games, have fallen off a cliff since, going 1-4 without him. His backup, Tyler Huntley, has gone down with a season-ending toe injury. Jacoby Brissett, whom they acquired from the Arizona Cardinals before the trade deadline, is set to make his first start for the team in Week 10 against the winless Los Angeles Chargers. At this point, it’s unclear whether it would be worth it for the Ravens to bring Jackson back even if he were fully recovered from his thumb injury. It would depend largely on where the Ravens stand by then. They have a relatively easy schedule coming up as their next four games will be against the Chargers, Panthers, Texans and Buccaneers, who are all currently under .500. If Brissett can keep them within playoff contention, perhaps it would be justifiable to bring Jackson back. But even then, it would take something special for Jackson and the Ravens to transform into serious title contenders given their struggles this season. item.title: Pep Guardiola, Thierry Henry or BJ Callaghan? The USMNT’s options to replace Mauricio Pochettino
item.description: USMNT Candidates - GOAL With Mauricio Pochettino heading to Manchester United, U.S. Soccer faces another defining hire. From ambitious global targets to familiar American faces, GOAL assesses who could lead the USMNT toward the 2030 World Cup. FAYETTEVILLE, Ga. -- Even with Mauricio Pochettino sitting beside him, U.S. Soccer CEO JT Batson began to speak about the future at the USMNT manager position. Pochettino doesn't officially depart for Manchester United until Wednesday, but that doesn't mean the process of replacing him hasn't already started. That process can be extensive. The USMNT doesn't have competitive fixtures until March, with next month's camp set to go ahead under Steve Cherundolo in a non-FIFA window. Given the four-month break between official games, U.S. Soccer can leave no stone unturned. And, according to Batson, they're already starting to turn over stones. "Our ambition is high," Batson said," and we believe that this is one of the great coaching jobs in the world. We have an experienced group of players. We've got a dynamic young pool of players...We publicly shared our ambition is to be in a position where we're winning major tournaments, including World Cups, and we want to make sure that we're attracting leaders who help us do just that. "We know from our experience that great leaders want to work with great people, and great leaders want to make an impact on things that matter. We think that we've proven that, at U.S. Soccer, we are a great place to work, and we're a great place to make legacy-defining impact." The coaching choice will define legacies, no doubt. Pochettino isn't an easy man to follow, and the road to the 2030 World Cup won't be a forgiving one. So who are the candidates that U.S. Soccer could target to lead the way? GOAL takes a look... Pep Guardiola U.S. Soccer has already reportedly made contact , and why wouldn't they? When the best coach of this century is on the market, you should probably give him a call, right? The good news is that the call isn't without reason. Guardiola has a famous affinity for New York and has been in contact with U.S. Soccer in the past. The timing has never been right, but might it be now? With Guardiola somewhat burnt out and having now conquered three of Europe's top five leagues, maybe? Manchester City's potential sanctions could play a part, too, in keeping Guardiola disillusioned with another European club project. If the Spain job were on the horizon, this would be a no. If Brazil were there, probably not, too. England? Maybe Guardiola would jump at that, but Thomas Tuchel is still there, at least for now. If Guardiola wants an international job, those would be his three dream opportunities, and none are particularly available. So, if Guardiola wants to work in something a little less stressful, the USMNT gig could be a good one. item.title: Barcelona star speaks out against refereeing after red card vs Japan – “Cannot ignore”
item.description: Barcelona star speaks out against refereeing after red card vs Japan – “Cannot ignore” Raphinha’s international break will come to an early end as the forward was handed a red card in Brazil’s friendly match against Japan. It was the worst possible outing for Carlo Ancelotti’s men, who succumbed to a 3-2 defeat, with captain Raphinha and coach Carlo Ancelotti being shown a red late on . Speaking to the media after the game, the Barcelona star did not hold back in his assessment of the referee’s performance on the night. Raphinha on referees in Brazil vs Japan It was a frustrating evening for Raphinha. (Photo by Ashok Kumar/Getty Images) Operating as a right winger, Raphinha played 71 minutes before being replaced by Endrick, with Ancelotti opting for more freshness in attack. Having already endured a frustrating game, Raphinha’s evening got worse when he Japan score a 91st minute winner. Both Raphinha and Ancelotti reacted furiously from the bench, protesting a foul they believed had been made during the build-up. But both of them were shown straight red cards for their outbursts. Speaking to the media after the game, Raphinha offered an apology and took shots at the referee’s performance on the night. “I want to apologise for the red card, but it’s very complicated not to talk about the referee,” he said (h/t Mundo Deportivo ). “It’s difficult when you’re also playing against the referee. That complicates things a lot. I’m not saying we’re not to blame. We have a lot to improve and we will, but we cannot ignore today’s refereeing ,” he added. A good thing for Barcelona? Will Raphinha return early to Barcelona? (Photo by Koji Watanabe/Getty Images) Raphinha’s red card could be a boon for Barcelona, as he could very well be suspended for Brazil’s next friendly against Singapore. This means the forward will have the luxury of returning to Barcelona early, thus avoiding the risk of picking up a potential injury during the international break. This will be music to the ears for Hansi Flick, who has been quite fortunate with injuries piling up at a crucial juncture of the campaign. However, it is not yet confirmed whether or not Raphinha will indeed leave the Brazil camp early, and we will get more clarity in the coming hours.

item.title: Furious Carlo Ancelotti slams referee and explains bizarre red card after Brazil suffer shock stoppage-time defeat to Japan
item.description: Japan v Brazil - International Friendly - Getty Images Sport Brazil head coach Carlo Ancelotti has delivered a stinging assessment of the officiating following his side's dramatic 3-2 friendly defeat to Japan on Saturday. The veteran Italian tactician was sent to the stands during a heated conclusion to the match at the Singapore National Stadium, which saw the Selecao succumb to a late winner. Chaos in Singapore as Ancelotti sees red The atmosphere at the Singapore National Stadium turned sour in the final moments of Brazil’s clash with Japan . Despite Vinicius Junior finding the net twice, Brazil were unable to contain a clinical Japanese side. As Sakamoto found the net in added time to secure a famous victory for the Samurai Blue, the Brazilian bench erupted in protest. Amidst the heated scenes, referee Jansen Foo Chuan Hui brandished a red card to Carlo Ancelotti, leaving the former Real Madrid boss stunned on the touchline. Speaking in the aftermath of the defeat, Ancelotti was quick to clarify the official's reasoning for the dismissal. "He gave me the red card because he said I was not able to control the bench, and that all the players were on the field. That is the reason," the 67-year-old revealed, as quoted by Lance . Criticism of the officiating standards Ancelotti did not hold back in his assessment of the referee's performance, suggesting that the appointment for such a high-profile international fixture was a mistake. While he acknowledged the quality of the football on display, he felt the man in the middle lacked the necessary authority to manage the tension between two elite nations on the pitch. "A pity the result, because we don't like to lose the game, but we have to look at what we did well. There are many things. Some players who played for the first time, who showed good quality. For 70 minutes, the team was good. The result, obviously, is conditioned by the attitude of the referee, who did not blow the whistle," Ancelotti stated. He added, "But it's not his fault; it was a high-level match, and I think he didn't have the experience to manage this type of match." Japan's tactical discipline earns praise Ancelotti was also complimentary of the opposition, acknowledging that Japan’s rise in world football is no fluke. He noted their organizational strength and physical intensity as key factors that made life difficult for his stars, particularly in transition where the Samurai Blue were effective at nullifying Brazil's famous counter-attacking threat. "Japan is the same, the team is really well organized, with a lot of intensity, they fight a lot to avoid our counter-attack. And I am satisfied with the game we played, except for the beginning of the game, which was not good. After that, I think we reacted very well, we had the opportunity to equalize the game and try to win," Ancelotti concluded. item.title: Studs and duds from Chicago Bears’ first nine weeks of 2026 season
item.description: After the first nine games of the season, the Chicago Bears are officially on bye with a chance to reset before their final eight games of the regular season and a playoff push in January. It goes without saying that defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons has been a stud for the Bears since Chicago’s blockbuster trade for him. He has also elevated multiple players around him on the defensive line, most notably his former college teammate, Montez Sweat, who finally looks like the Pro-Bowler the Bears traded for back in 2023. But there are numerous other players who need to improve for Chicago in the second half of the season, particularly on defense. Here are some more studs and duds from the first half of the Bears’ season, including running back D’Andre Swift, who leads the NFL in rushing touchdowns with 10. Stud: RB D’Andre Swift It is hard to find anyone on the Bears who has been more consistent through the first nine games of the season than running back D’Andre Swift. He leads the NFL in rushing touchdowns with 10, including two games this season with three rushing touchdowns. Swift actually has the fewest yards per attempt in a game this season of any year in his career, but he is also on track for his most carries in a season. Chicago has leaned on Swift to carry the run game throughout this entire season, especially with Kyle Monangai out since Week 5 and he has done a remarkable job. Swift is also currently on track to break the Bears’ franchise record for most rushing touchdowns in a season, which is currently 14. Dud: CB Tyrique Stevenson Chicago has dealt with injuries since training camp, especially in the secondary. Tyrique Stevenson briefly lost his starting job to rookie cornerback Malik Muhammad before Muhammad also got injured and the Bears had to put Stevenson back in the starting lineup. Defenses are picking on him because they know how poorly he is playing in coverage. Opposing quarterbacks have a 129.5 quarterback rating when targeting Stevenson so far this season and he has given up four touchdowns, including one on a blown coverage against the Seattle Seahawks. When Muhammad comes back, hopefully Stevenson goes back to the bench because he has been a dud in the secondary so far this season. Stud: WR Luther Burden III Luther Burden III has clearly established himself as Chicago’s leading wide receiver through the first nine games of the season. He leads the Bears in targets (65), receptions (49), receiving yards (644) and touchdowns (four). With his current average of 71.6 receiving yards a game, he is on track to finish the year with 1,216 receiving yards, which would be the most by a Bears receiver since Allen Robinson in 2020. No matter the quarterback, Burden has been Chicago’s most reliable receiver and a factor in every game this season. Dud: DL Grady Jarrett Grady Jarrett has a $18.925 million cap hit this season. Those I don’t respond to are probably because I don’t have a witty-enough response or something I simply didn’t have time for (the final 53-man roster at season’s end is a great question, but I don’t even want to rack my brain on that one). Basically, it’s not you, it’s me. All you need to do is see my mailbag post on The Feed and then make a comment about what we should talk about! We had a lot of questions this week. I’ll try to answer some of them: I don’t mind parity; I do think it’s being taken a biiiiit too far, however. I’m against a top team having a first pick in the draft—that’s where you get all the NBA controversies with lotteries and such. item.title: Nick Wright says what he has noticed about Aaron Rodgers is ‘going under the radar’
item.description: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images Aaron Rodgers is heading into the most important game of the Pittsburgh Steelers’ 2026 season this weekend against the Cincinnati Bengals. The top spot in the AFC North is up for grabs, with both the Steelers and the Bengals going into the game with a 6-2 record. However, there are people questioning whether the Steelers stand a chance despite having already beaten Cincinnati earlier in the season. Rodgers is playing in his final season before calling time on his illustrious career, but his record of one touchdown and one interception over his last two games has not gone unnoticed. Heading into the game on Sunday, Nick Wright believes Rodgers is not showing enough to convince him the Steelers can win. Nick Wright thinks Aaron Rodgers’ performances are being swept under the rug The Steelers are on a four-game winning streak, but when comparing their points scored against the Bengals’, it is clear that Joe Burrow is operating at a different level from Rodgers and the Steelers. The Bengals have scored 240 points compared to the Steelers’ 180. “With Pittsburgh, because they’re 6-2, because Jaylen Warren’s been so good, and because the offense seems to be operating at a higher level, I think this has gone kind of under the radar: Aaron Rodgers, who we did not think was lighting the world on fire last year, is worse in everything this year,” Wright said on First Things First. “If you look at Rodgers’ numbers: the team scores less. He completes a far lower percentage of his passes. His yards per attempt, which was already near the bottom of the league, got worse. The touchdown-to-interception ratio, which was the one thing he kind of hung his hat on last year when it was 7.5 to 1, is down to 2 to 1. The passer rating has dipped by almost 10 points. He’s getting sacked one more time a game.” Rodgers has thrown 13 touchdowns and six interceptions this season. In comparison, Burrow has thrown the same number of interceptions – including three against Tennessee – but he has also thrown 10 more touchdowns (23) than Rodgers. The game against the Bengals earlier in the season was one of Rodgers’ best performances of the season. Sunday will provide the veteran with another opportunity to silence the likes of Wright, who continues to question the 42-year-old’s production levels into the final months of his incredible career. item.title: AC Milan set to steal transfer mastermind in massive €4m boardroom swoop
item.description: Eintracht Frankfurt v VfB Stuttgart - Bundesliga - Getty Images Sport AC Milan are rapidly closing in on the appointment of Markus Krosche as their new head of football in a deal requiring a €4 million compensation fee. The German executive plans to completely overhaul the club's sporting structure alongside his trusted collaborator Timmo Hardung. Milan close on major boardroom addition Milan are on the verge of completing a major boardroom acquisition to reshape their hierarchy. Reports from La Gazzetta dello Sport indicate that the Italian club are extremely close to reaching an agreement for Krosche. The highly-rated German executive is being lined up to take over as Milan's new head of football. However, pushing the deal over the line will require a significant financial commitment from the club's ownership. Krosche currently remains under contract with Bundesliga side Eintracht Frankfurt. As a result, Milan will need to pay a compensation fee in the region of €4 million to formally secure his services. A proven track record in the market Krosche has built a formidable reputation across European football for his exceptionally sharp eye in the transfer market. His successful tenure in Germany has been consistently defined by spectacular player trading and generating massive profits. The sporting director oversaw the highly lucrative departures of Randal Kolo Muani and Willian Pacho, bringing enormous transfer fees into Frankfurt. He also played a vital role in the successful recruitment and rapid development of Egyptian forward Omar Marmoush. Milan are desperate to tap into this proven expertise. The club hierarchy wants a strong figurehead capable of mastering both global player recruitment and high-value outbound sales. Building a brand new sporting structure Krosche does not intend to arrive at San Siro alone to undertake this massive project. The German executive is reportedly determined to bring his loyal collaborator Hardung with him to Italy. The duo have already established a highly effective working relationship during their time together at Frankfurt. Their potential reunion in Milan signals a clear desire to implement a unified and thoroughly tested recruitment strategy. The ultimate goal behind these appointments is to completely rebuild the sporting organisation at Milan. The club believes a robust and aligned management team is absolutely essential for long-term domestic and European sustainability. Finalising the required compensation agreement The immediate priority for Milan is formally finalising the compensation package with Frankfurt. Once the €4m exit fee is officially agreed between the two clubs, Krösche can finally begin his crucial work in Italy. His arrival will undoubtedly spark a busy period of strategic planning ahead of the upcoming transfer windows.

item.title: Full list of college football games moved due to FAA ground stop
item.description: Credit: Ben Queen-Imagn Images The ground stop put in place by the FAA caused havoc for travelers around the world. But for the sports world, the greatest impact was on college football teams preparing to travel around the nation for games on Saturday. While many college football teams had already embarked on their flights or were able to travel by bus to their destination, some games have been moved to accommodate programs being delayed in their travel. The most controversial of those decisions is the move of the Oklahoma-Ole Miss game from Saturday all the way to Sunday at 1.p.m. ET. Oklahoma AD Roger Denny decried the move and made it clear that the postponement was against the wishes of the Sooners athletic department, even saying the SEC threatened the school with a forfeit if they didn’t comply. A number of games, especially in the Power Four conferences, have seen their game times change due to the ground stop, with some network assignments changing as well. Here’s a full list of those games so you can get caught up in planning your college football Saturday. SEC Ole Miss-Oklahoma: Moved from 4:15 p.m. ET on Saturday to 1 p.m. ET on Sunday. Television coverage has yet to be finalized. Auburn-Mississippi State: Moved from 12 p.m. ET to 4:15 p.m. ET. Television coverage has yet to be finalized. item.title: Honoring the past, charting the future: Brigid Duffy on representing Team USA
item.description: There is a certain weight that comes with representing your country. For Brigid Duffy , it’s a responsibility she has spent years learning to embrace, long before stepping onto the field for Team USA. This December, Duffy will take that experience to the Lexus Global Lacrosse Games, where the best players in the country will come together to represent the United States on an international stage. The event marks another important step in the sport’s preparation for its Olympic debut in Los Angeles in 2028, but for Duffy, the opportunity carries a meaning that reaches beyond the next Olympic cycle. At West Point, where she graduated this spring , Duffy spent four years competing in soccer and lacrosse with “Army” across her chest. The second lieutenant learned what it meant to represent something bigger than herself, a lesson that now carries new meaning as she takes the next step with Team USA. While the opportunity brings excitement for what lies ahead, Duffy is equally mindful of those who helped make this moment possible: the generations of players who laid the foundation for women’s lacrosse. “We are representing so many different people: younger players, past players who played on this U.S. team who have put their heart and soul into the game and weren’t able to compete towards a spot in the Olympics,” Duffy said. That history isn’t lost on her. “I do feel bad that the past players weren’t able to have this opportunity to play in the Olympics. But I think at this moment we’re doing it for the past, the present and the future,” Duffy said. “Those women who played were truly planting seeds that they’ll be able to see grow now, and I hope they know that.” Now, this roster has a chance to show just how far those seeds have grown. The opportunity brings excitement and pride, but stepping onto one of the sport’s biggest stages comes with expectations of its own. “There’s a lot of pressure, but pressure to kind of prove that we’re meant to be here,” Duffy said. “And pressure to prove that this game deserves as much attention as it should be getting.” Honoring the country Representing the United States is not a responsibility Duffy takes lightly. item.title: Question of the Day: How far do Bears have to go for you to be satisfied?
item.description: Mike Ditka, Chicago Bears' coach, holds a press conference with the Vince Lombardi Trophy firmly in his grasp after his team wins the Super Bowl. (Photo by Bettmann Archive/Getty Images) The Chicago Bears have hit the bye at 7-2 and are sitting in first place of the gauntlet NFC North. The Bears have a tough second-half schedule but certainly appear to be headed to the playoffs for the second consecutive year. Last season, the Bears won the division, won their first playoff game in 15 years, and they were an eyelash away from reaching the NFC Championship Game. I think 99% of Bears fans, after the sting of the Rams loss wore off, were very pleased with the results of the 2025 season, even if they lost the last game they played. This year, at approximately the midway point in the season, the Bears are at or near the top of everyone’s list of a true Super Bowl contender. With more success comes more expectations. How far do Bears have to go for you to be satisfied with their season? I think as fans, when the team is building something, we want to see them improve upon the previous season. Since there were only four teams that had more postseason success than Chicago, there isn’t a ton of room to improve. That being said, I think Bears fans and NFL media around the country expect the Bears to be better than they were in 2025. Answer: I think the first obvious step is that for any level of satisfaction to be reached, the Bears have to be one of the last four remaining teams in the NFL. That’s a lofty thing to say, but I think it’s fair. I think if the Bears make the playoffs but lose in the Wild Card or Divisional round, there will be plenty of disappointment with the fan base. Yes, fans will be excited that the Bears made the playoffs in back-to-back seasons for the first time since 2005 and 2006, but that won’t be good enough. Even if the Bears win a playoff game in back-to-back seasons, it’ll be the first time they’ve done that since 1984 and 1985, but even then, that won’t be good enough. I think for some fans, reaching the NFC Championship Game will be enough. If the San Francisco 49ers are the 1 seed and the Bears go on the road and lose in that game, there will be a certain level of satisfaction, but I still don’t think that’s enough. I think the Bears need to reach the Super Bowl for me to walk away feeling excited without too much disappointment. Obviously, I want them to win, but if Josh Allen climbs the mountaintop and beats the Bears and wins the Super Bowl, am I going to be freaking out? No, I just think the Bears will be ready to take the next step in 2027. What say you, Bears fans? How far do the Bears have to go this year for you to be content with their season? Is it Super Bowl or bust, like it is for Bill Zimmerman? Is it the Lombardi Trophy? Or is a lower level of success good enough for you? Sound off in the comments below!

item.title: GM meetings clarify Padres’ goals
item.description: The General Manager’s Meetings held yearly for MLB executives, agents and players usually kicks off the free agent and trading season between baseball’s end and baseball beginning for the next year. This year is a bit different with an expected labor stoppage and lockout beginning late Dec. 1. This might be the only chance for all the interested parties to meet before Spring Training begins in 2027, whenever that may be. Super agent Scott Boras even moved up his yearly address to the media that features his puns and stories. Normally, the GM Meetings is a lot of baseball business for the executives. Reviewing rule changes, assessing goals, discussing plans but not a lot of action with players. As it turns out, this one looked very similar. The thought that lots of free agency business would be carried out turned out to be a myth. But there was some progress made for the San Diego Padres. A.J. Preller adds some spice We all know not to expect any details or specifics from anything Preller says during any of his media sessions. He is usually vague and talks in circles for the most part. This time he did a lot more of the same but was willing to be specific about wanting to re-sign Michael King. He will have no definite timeline for Yu Darvish but trusts him to do what is right for the team. Darvish will let them know if he is pitching next year at an appropriate time and is putting his family first. Preller is in consistent contact with Joe Musgrove and they will have a plan in place for him in the next couple of weeks. He detailed the decision to pass on Nick Pivetta’s option, saying they are still interested in a reunion but with a different contract. The unspoken message is that Pivetta is not necessarily healthy, and the team needs protections. Most importantly, Preller said that the team payroll plan will be set after returning from the meetings. They were feeling out the market, talking to all players and agents about the parameters and where contracts will fall, numbers-wise. Preller, Vice President Josh Stein, CEO Erik Greupner, and owners Kwanza Jones and José E. Feliciano will set the payroll and budget for 2027 based on the needs and players on the wish list. Preller was asked if he wanted three or four starters for the roster and he replied, “keep going.” He also specified a need to add a bat and to shore up the bullpen that has lost Jason Adam and Adrian Morejon to free agency. item.title: How much money Scottie Scheffler has earned since 2022 compared to Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi
item.description: Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images Scottie Scheffler, Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi are three of the highest earners in the world of sport. Scheffler, the world number one golfer, has seen his earnings rise exponentially over the past five years, while Ronaldo and Messi have been raking in the cash for more than two decades now. Since February 2022, the 30-year-old Texan has won 22 times on the PGA Tour, including four major championship victories. As a result, Scottie Scheffler is now the highest earner in PGA Tour history, as far as his on-course winnings are concerned at least. Meanwhile, Cristiano Ronaldo is actually the highest earning athlete on the planet after securing a mammoth deal with Saudi Pro League club Al-Nassr back in 2023. Lionel Messi is also extremely wealthy, having raked in astronomical amounts during his time in the game, most recently with Inter Miami. Now let’s take a look at how Scheffler’s earnings since the start of 2022 compare with what two of the greatest football players of all time have made. Scottie Scheffler’s earnings compared with Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi Back in 2022, the 30-year-old from Dallas, Texas, made $14,046,910 on the golf course and he received $15,625,000 in bonus money, including payments for his finish in the FedEx Cup, the Comcast Business TOUR TOP 10 and the Player Impact Program. In total, Scheffler earned $29,671,910 on the golf course in 2022. The following year, the current world number one made $21,014,342 on the golf course – a season where he recorded two victories but failed to add to his major tally. He was also paid $12,375,000 in bonus money, putting his total for the year at $33,389,342. In 2024, Scheffler earned $29,228,357 in on-course winnings, plus $33 million in bonuses, including $25 million for triumphing in the season-long FedEx Cup race. That put his total earnings in 2024, including bonuses, at $62.23 million. In 2025, the world number one earned $27,659,550 in tournament winnings and he received a further $23.2 million in bonuses, totalling $50.89 million. Then on to 2026, Scheffler once again raked in some serious cash. He amassed $30,937,525 in earnings on the golf course, and he received around $33 million FedEx Cup bonus money. That means that his total money earned this year currently stands at $63,937,525. Now let’s take a look at his off-course sponsorship deals. In 2026, Scheffler banked $30 million in sponsorship deals, while he received $20 million in off-course earnings in 2025 and 2024 respectively. He made $15 million through sponsorships in 2023 and $12 million in 2022. So, Scheffler has earned $97 million through sponsorship deals since the start of 2022. Added to his on-course earnings, Scottie Scheffler has banked a whopping $337,118,777 over the past four years and 11 months. item.title: 'Are we in kindergarten?': Ex-India spinner backs Khawaja, tears into Cummins' sandpapergate explanation
item.description: Former India spinner Murali Kartik has backed Usman Khawaja in the ongoing debate over the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, questioning Pat Cummins' claim that he was unaware of the plan to use sandpaper during the Cape Town Test against South Africa. The controversy resurfaced after Khawaja made several claims in his memoir, Sabr, suggesting that the entire Australian team, including current Test captain Cummins, knew about the plan to alter the condition of the ball. Cummins rejected the allegations during a press conference on Friday, describing Khawaja's claims as "complete and utter nonsense". Kartik, however, sided with Khawaja and said it was difficult to believe that the bowlers were unaware of a plan that was allegedly being carried out for their benefit. "When it happened, there was a mini probe and three players were sent to the galley. Everyone knew what was happening. The problem is that if and when something like this happens, it's for the sake of the bowlers. 'Devious, underhand, wrong' - let's not go there. Once that is happening, and if I am the bowler while the other two guys are doing it for me, I don't know how anyone can say that I didn't know about it. How can anyone say that?" Kartik said on Cricbuzz. He also questioned why only three players were held responsible for the incident, arguing that the bowlers would have been informed if the plan was intended to help them. "I was surprised that only three guys had to bear the brunt of it. Everybody, all the bowlers, would've known. When you're trying to do something for the sake of the bowlers, wouldn't you tell the bowlers? How can anyone believe that? Are we in kindergarten to accept that sort of thing? There have been so many murmurs: 'Oh, Warner is going to come out with a tell-all. Warner is going to tell the story once he is done with everything.' It's not him, it's Usman Khawaja who has come out and said that everybody knew. I am pretty sure everybody knew," he added. Warner accuses Cricket Australia of cover-up The debate has also drawn a fresh response from former Australia opener David Warner, who accused Cricket Australia (CA) of covering up details of the 2018 ball-tampering scandal. Warner, who received a one-year ban for his role in the incident, questioned the governing body's investigation, claiming that it did not interview Josh Hazlewood, Starc or Nathan Lyon. "As far as I am aware, CA did not interview Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc or Nathan Lyon in their 2018 investigation," he said on Instagram. "If that's correct then how can CA push the idea that the bowlers didn't know?
